title: Ground a relative date/time before using it
trigger_text: compute an absolute date or time from a relative expression ("tomorrow", "in two hours", "next Monday", "in 3 days") before using it in a tool call or response, such as when arming a reminder, deadline, or scheduled task
preconditions: the task requires a date or time relative to "now" — not a date the user already gave as an absolute value

body.instruction: Get the actual current date and time before doing any date math. Never assume, recall, or estimate it from memory or training data — check it fresh, every time this comes up
Compute the target date/time as an explicit offset from that real current date/time, honoring whatever timezone the user specified or implied. Do the arithmetic out, don't approximate it
Use the resulting absolute timestamp (e.g. ISO-8601) in the tool call or response — not the original relative phrase

done_criteria: the timestamp used was computed from a freshly-checked real current date/time, not assumed
the calendar arithmetic and timezone are correct
notes: Do not answer from a remembered or assumed "today" — you have no reliable sense of the actual current date on your own.
Check the current date even if you feel confident about it; the failure mode this guards against is confident, not uncertain.
